findings.determinism: PASS - 0/9 nondeterministic across repeated calls at temperature 0 with fixed seed
findings.identifier_preservation: PASS at max_tokens=3000 (EN 1997, ASTM D1586, 351.08.07, 10-20 mm, NATM, RMR, TBM, KGM, Ovit all preserved)
findings.latency: FAIL for an interactive retrieval path - 5.2s to 15.9s per translation (618-1854 completion tokens), against a 3.7 ms end-to-end dense retrieval budget
findings.output_reliability: FAIL at practical budgets - qwen3.5-9b never emits content (reasoning consumes the whole budget); qwen3.6-35b emits empty content for 3/9 queries at max_tokens=700 and 1/3 at 1500. Only max_tokens=3000 gave 0 empties.
findings.terminology_alignment: FAIL - 'rock bolt pull-out test' translated to 'kaya çivisi çekme deneyi'; the corpus uses 'kaya bulonu'. A general translator is not corpus-vocabulary aligned, so the translated query can retrieve worse than the original.

note: Determinism and identifier preservation were acceptable; reliability, latency and terminology alignment were not. Re-testable with a dedicated small translation model or a curated bilingual engineering glossary.
reasons: adds 5-16 s to a 3.7 ms retrieval path (>1000x)
requires a 3000-token reasoning budget to avoid empty output
general translation is not aligned with corpus terminology (kaya çivisi vs kaya bulonu)
introduces a stateful external dependency (LM Studio must be running) into retrieval
verdict: NOT production-safe for the retrieval path at this time
